script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The explanation repeats the unpaid-work point three times without adding much. It sounds flat and mechanical.
After giving the LORD’s question, the explanation repeats that it is His question and that it concerns kingship. It sounds flat and generic.
The verse calls them poor and needy, but does not say they were the people who needed justice most.
Saying everything he looks at and wants lands on his own gain leaves out the other things his eyes and heart are set on in the same verse.
Calling dishonest gain his whole focus leaves out the other things named in verse 17. The statement about what his father cared about also assigns him a feeling the text does not state.
The verse says they will not mourn for him. Saying no one will cry for him broadens that statement beyond what it says.
The verse says they will not mourn for him with those cries. Saying no one will say them broadens that statement beyond what it says.
The verse names Lebanon, Bashan and Abarim as places for the cry, but does not specify the mountains of all three.
The verse calls for crying out from those places; it does not say the cry is heard from them.
Saying nobody woke up one morning and decided to refuse adds a claim about how the disobedience began. The text says it has been the way from youth.
The final sentence is confusing: it does not make clear why Papa is glad the image comes as a question or how the next verse relates to that.
Calling the instruction to enroll Coniah as childless the last word on him overlooks the rest of the same verse, which speaks about his descendants.
